newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-MOYA BLASTS CHANG OUT OF OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-MOYA BLASTS CHANG OUT OF OPEN.

text.p: Unseeded Spaniard Carlos Moya was once more the giant-killer at the Australian Open on Thursday, beating world number two Michael Chang of the United States for a place in Sunday's men's final.
Moya, who ousted defending champion Boris Becker in the first round of the tournament, beat Chang 7-5 6-2 6-4 in just over two hours.
Chang, who has not won a grand slam title since lifting the French Open as a 17-year-old in 1989, had played the most consistent tennis of any major name in Melbourne.
But the tall, languid 20-year-old from Barcelona seemed unimpressed with his opponent's reputation, sending fierce backhand and forehand drives past Chang from the outset.

Chang showed rare moments of emotion and stared repeatedly at his racquet as the confident Moya, who saw off a final-set challenge, headed to victory. Moya thrust his arms in the air and saluted the crowd after sealing the win.

Moya becomes the first Spanish male in the finals of the year's first grand slam since Andres Gimeno lost to the great Rod Laver in 1969. He will meet either world number one Pete Sampras or fifth-seeded Austrian Thomas Muster in Sunday's final.
